docs.title: City of Exiles
docs.text:
Welcome to the world of Erratt — a land still bleeding from the Schism, the day the Feywild tried to fold itself into the material plane. Magic and Fey spilled across the world, the ground itself was split, and the beasts of the forests woke into thought. Every border, grudge, and alliance that follows was drawn in that wound's shadow.

Our story begins at the edge of the map, in Utsa Paradisa — the Jewel of the Desert, the City of Exiles. It is a walled oasis where water is sacred because it is scarce, and where the cast-out of a hundred dead nations have come to build something like a home. This is the session archive and campaign wiki: a record of who the exiles are, what they've done, and the world that keeps testing them.

docs.title: The Schism
docs.text: The Schism was no war and no plague — it was the moment two worlds nearly became one. When the Feywild pressed against the material plane, it tore the land apart, flooded Erratt with raw magic and Fey denizens, and awakened ordinary forest animals into the sentient Beastfolk. The great powers that survived did so by adapting: dwarves and orcs ended centuries of mountain war with the Iron Grey Concordat, Drathomir carved new territory from the ashes of the Deadwood, and the Eladrin — blamed for it all — have been mistrusted ever since. Nothing in Erratt is untouched by it.

docs.title: The City of Exiles
docs.text:
Utsa Paradisa is home to those who could go nowhere else: predominantly Tieflings shunned by nations that no longer exist, a large Tabaxi population, and other exiled beastfolk. Here, control of water is control of everything — it is guarded, rationed, and revered, its rites tended at the Water Temple and its peace kept by the City Guard. From the crowded Bazaar and the tortoise-shell homes of the Slums to the wealth of the Jade District and the halls of the University, it is a city of outcasts carving out belonging amid scarcity and prejudice.

Utsa Paradisa punches far above its size. Empress Serenity brokered the tenuous peace between Drathomir and the Goliaths, giving the city real diplomatic weight, and its lifeline runs north to UkRuundir, the Goliath capital — trading tar and spices for lumber and mammoth meat across a brutal desert-to-cold-forest crossing that few dare to make.

docs.title: The Wider World
docs.text: Beyond the desert lie the three great nations: cosmopolitan Trivan at the bottom of the Schism, the dwarven-and-orc Iron Holds, the dragonborn realm of Drathomir, and Medui-Ghislerin, the elven Tree of Five Families. Eastward stretch the Riverlands and the Emerald Wilderness, tended by halflings and firbolgs; northward, past Utsa Paradisa, sprawl the untamed Northern Territories. It is a crowded, quarrelsome world of old grudges and older gods — and the exiles are only just stepping into it.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text: # Session Date 1 The Tidewoven Amulet July 3, 2026 2 The Vanished Scholars August 11, 2026

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: With Utsa Paradisa still reeling from a citywide assault, the party fought through the Slums and the Jade District to beat back an invasion of fey and elemental creatures. They saved a district and a family — but arrived at the Water Temple too late to stop the abduction of the water priestess Naivara Tidewoven, who left behind a talking amulet that would set the party's next quest in motion.

docs.title: Key Events
docs.text:
• Aftermath and triage. In the ransacked Bazaar, the party freed Major Jamieson, a guard the suture flies had stitched together — hands sewn to his thighs, lips sewn shut — through a tense run of medicine checks and healing. The Major swore that his fellow guard Charles Dammit, who fled the fight, would be scrubbing his office when it was over.
  • Choosing the fight. The Griffin rider Seris flew an aerial recon (natural 20) and laid out the city's wounds: the University held, the Slums were battered, and the Jade District — home of the Griffins and the Water Temple — was under the heaviest attack. Seris peeled off to defend her Griffins; the party marched on the Slums, drawn by Behnsun Payne's orphanage and Adarius's parents.
  • The battle for the Slums. Amid the tortoise-shell homes, the party fought magma mephits, suture flies, and a thirster. A mephit's breath cone caught Adarius's father — critically — and burned half his face, but the hardy man survived. Paddy Greenfoot and the Dragonborn Band — old rivals from a chariot race — turned up to buoy the party with inspiring music.
  • The Water Temple falls. Pressing on to the Jade District, the party found suture flies sewing Naivara Tidewoven's mouth and hands shut. Despite the veteran commander Dalen Marr's stand, the flies lifted the priestess and carried her out of the city.
  • The dropped clue. As she was flown away, Naivara left behind a gold teardrop amulet. Adarius's identify revealed "something trapped inside" — a fey being that rejected him outright ("you were not chosen") and turned to Prance Galavant: "You will do. You must save my daughter." Prance swore an oath to the Amulet Speaker, put the amulet on, and felt "a spark of magic click."

docs.title: Memorable Moments
docs.text:
• Death from above. The party spent whole turns building a catapult mid-battle — a natural-20 contraption — and used it twice: first flinging Prance across the field, then launching Krum some 80 feet through the air to crash down on a fire mephit, driving both daggers through it and squashing the creature into the cracked earth.
  • A 39-damage flourish. Prance's brutal-critical longsword swing, delivered mid-monologue — "only when it's most dramatic."
  • "Healing is my game." Behnsun Payne introduced himself to the freed Major Jamieson in rhyme, then later froze a fire mephit with a chromatic orb of cold.
  • Talking to furniture. Fizz held his amulet Frederick up to the new one and "made them kiss," drawing drops of water from the teardrop — and learned that he, too, had been "chosen."
  • The world's grumpiest quest-giver. The amulet snapping at Adarius: "I have feelings, and my daughter was just kidnapped. I'm having a bad day."

docs.title: Open Threads
docs.text:
• Where is Naivara Tidewoven? The suture flies carried her out of the city alive. Who sent them to silence a water-priestess — and to what end?
  • The amulet's nature. The Amulet Speaker claims to be Naivara's father, trapped in the teardrop. What is he, how was he bound, and what does it mean that both Prance and Fizz have been "chosen"?
  • Two chosen, two amulets. Frederick named the Tidewoven spirit a "brother" but admitted he isn't sure he trusts him. How are the two fey vessels — and their bearers — connected?
  • The city's attackers. The fey and elemental creatures were beaten back "for now," but no one learned who unleashed them.
  • Adarius's dissent. Adarius rolled his way to genuine conviction that the amulet is bad news and still wants to sell it. That fault line isn't resolved.

docs.title: The Scene
docs.text:
The catapult had already thrown Prance once, and the party — half-mad on the sheer audacity of it — had built the thing back up for another shot. Krum climbed into the sling without a word of complaint, because a dwarf does not complain about being turned into ammunition; a dwarf simply checks that his daggers are loose in their sheaths. Below him the Slums burned in patches, the hollowed tortoise-shell homes throwing long shadows across the dust, and out among them a fire mephit hovered on crackling wings, chuckling that small fiendish chuckle that had been fraying everyone's nerves for an hour. "On three," Fizz called, bracing the frame. Krum did not wait for three.

He went up and the world went quiet. For one long breath there was only wind and the thump of his own heart and the whole ruined district tilting beneath him — eighty feet of desert air with a burning imp at the bottom of it. The mephit looked up a half-second too late. It had time to widen its ember eyes and no time at all to move.

Krum came down like a dropped anvil with a grudge. Both daggers led the way, punched to the hilt through the creature's molten hide, and his full dwarven weight followed after — driving the thing straight down, flattening it into the cracked earth in a spray of sparks and a smell of burnt tar. The fire went out of it all at once, snuffed under a hundred and some pounds of rogue. Krum wrenched his blades free, stood up in the little crater he'd made, and dusted off his shoulders while the embers settled around his boots. Somewhere behind him, Prance was already announcing that this, too, would make a magnificent verse.

docs.title: The Vanished Scholars
docs.text: August 11, 2026

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: In the smoking aftermath of the assault, the party was led into the Jade Pyramid to report to Empress Serenity's council, where the rescue of the abducted priestess Naivara Tidewoven became Prance's sworn charge — and the University let slip that four of its brightest students had vanished in the chaos. Following that trail to the students' sealed dorm, the party tripped the missing diviner's trap: a mimic, a swarm of animated books, and a smothering rug that very nearly finished what the invaders had started.

docs.title: Key Events
docs.text:
• Into the pyramid. Dalen Marr and the hooded drow Velra led the party through a blood-keyed door and the Jade Pyramid's illusion-warped halls — corridors that fold and mislead — to the Empress's war room.
  • The council. The party met the city's powers all at once: Empress Serenity and her Goliath bodyguard Horace Steelwinter; the wine-soaked Salvatore Danilo of the Lucky Scorpion; the arena-owner Tirakar Sun; the Bazaar's Tisk Tisk; the University's Seris and Raasha Vaad; the Iron Holds' orc Gorvak Skybinder; and the guard leader Karza Sunhorn. Prance introduced the party with a booming flourish ("magnificent by necessity — now bow") and was immediately, publicly humbled by the Empress.
  • The charge. With the amulet whispering in his ear, Prance accepted the Empress's commission to bring Naivara back — "by blade and by my oath." The party won a guard escort in Krum; Adarius was promised a full University scholarship and a better home for his parents; and the Empress laid bare the stakes: without Naivara sanctifying the water, the dwindling supply turns deadly, and the attack's timing — on the eve of the Festival of the Four Currents — looked deliberate.
  • Four students gone. Pressed by the Empress, Seris and Raasha Vaad confessed a buried worry: four gifted students who shared an off-campus dorm — Cassian (evocation), Celine (divination), Varicash (illusion), and Calus (conjuration) — had vanished without a trace, their rooms showing no struggle and no detectable magic.
  • The University's dead. The party detoured to the University, still strewn with corpses, where Krum's battered uncle Holgren — who had lost some nine or ten students and fifteen guards — gave him a Gorgon-backed bronze mirror that revealed Krum's spectral Phantom self.
  • The trapped dorm. The "empty" room was warded by Celine's anti-divination devices — which is why earlier searches found nothing. As the party investigated, the furniture came alive: a mimic disguised as a desk, a swarm of flying books, and a smothering rug, all but immune to the party's psychic and charm magic. A brutal, unlucky fight followed; Krum and Adarius both dropped unconscious and were revived, and the session ended mid-battle, the exhausted party finally poised to take its long-overdue rest.

docs.title: Memorable Moments
docs.text:
• "Now bow." Prance's grandiose presentation of each companion in turn — "master of arriving precisely after the fight has begun" — capped by the Empress flatly telling him to speak when spoken to.
  • Fizz with the Rizz. Fizz charmed a 26 out of the suspicious Velra, who answered by licking his blood off her ring-hand and later pressing a dagger to his throat: "you should not trust anyone, my dear mushroom — but I think you may be worth my time." He talked Horace out of a fistful of healing potions on another 26.
  • The tango. Prance begged the festival's last dance and drew Horace Steelwinter himself, who — on a natural 20 — spun the rabbit-knight so hard he ended up tail-up on the floor while Prance flubbed his own step with a natural 1.
  • A salty bedside manner. Prance treated uncle Holgren's wounds with an "old fey remedy" that turned out to be a fistful of salt poured straight into the gash.
  • Death by furniture. Having survived mummies, suture flies, and fire mephits, the party was nearly wiped out by books and a rug — reduced at last to shoving a still-thrashing book into a drawer and holding it shut, then having Fizz decompose and eat the defeated volumes.

docs.title: Open Threads
docs.text:
• Who took Naivara — and why now? The abduction, the timing against the festival, and the missing students increasingly look like one plan, not three.
  • The four scholars. Why these four — one master of each school? Where did they go, and was the diviner Celine a victim or a conspirator, given the anti-divination wards and lethal guardians left in her own dorm?
  • The Iron Holds' hand. A promised water shipment never arrived, and the Empress openly suspects Gorvak Skybinder's masters of striking to make the city dependent. Coincidence, or cause?
  • Salvatore's offer. Salvatore Danilo whispered a job to Behnsun Payne — "I may have work for you." What kind?
  • Loose in the city. Tirakar Sun's arena lost monsters and prisoners in the attack; they're still out there. And the deserter Charles Dammit remains unaccounted for.
  • Krum's mirror. What is the Gorgon-backed glass, and what does the spectral double it shows portend?
  • Velra and Fizz. Trust, appraisal, or a blade waiting to fall?

docs.title: The Scene
docs.text:
It had been the longest day of their lives — eighteen hours of mummies and suture flies and fire that walked like men — and now, in a dead student's candlelit dorm, the furniture tried to finish them. The desk unhinged its jaw and a grey tongue lashed out to coil around Krum, hauling the dwarf off his feet and dragging him into a mouth that stank of old glue and acid; he sawed at it with both daggers and it only chewed harder. Books rose off the shelves in a fluttering swarm and dove like paper hawks, spines snapping shut on skulls, and a book — a book — cracked Behnsun across the head hard enough to drop him to one knee. Across the room the great jade-and-gold carpet peeled itself off the floor and reared up behind Adarius, and for all his humming and his blade-song footwork it caught him at last and folded him into its weight, wrapping tight until the world went dark and airless and his own heartbeat filled his ears.

Nothing worked the way it should. Adarius's shadow-blade sank into the rug and did nothing — psychic, wasted; Fizz's honeyed suggestions slid off inanimate paper that could not be charmed; his vicious mockery found a thing with no mind to wound. They were scattered to the four corners of a room barely wider than a hallway, each pinned to a different horror, unable to bring their fire to bear on any single one, and the dice ran cold as the grave — miss after miss after miss while the natural twenties fell like rain on the other side of the table. Krum went down. Adarius went down. Prance emptied the last of his lay on hands into the dwarf's chest to drag him back from the edge, then turned and, out of options and dignity both, simply grabbed the book savaging him, wrestled the snapping thing across the room, and stuffed it into a dresser drawer, sitting on it to keep it shut.

When at last the final volume gave up its stitched-together life, the room fell quiet but for torn pages settling and five heroes wheezing on the floorboards. Fizz looked at the shredded rug, the split desk, the drift of ruined books, and — being a mushroom, and past caring — set about decomposing them, urinating on the lot and then eating what was left, spores and all. Somewhere in the wreckage was a soft bed with his name on it. They had survived the sack of a city and the monsters that sacked it; they had, very nearly, been killed by a library. "Hope y'all had a good time," the room seemed to say, "despite getting your ass whooped by furniture." They found the beds, and they slept.

docs.title: City Guard of Utsa Paradisa
docs.text: The guardsmen who keep order in Utsa Paradisa — stretched perilously thin during the citywide assault, and holding the city's districts by their fingernails.

docs.title: Notable Members
docs.text:
• Major Jamieson — an officer rallying the guard at the Bazaar after the party freed him from the suture flies.
  • Dalen Marr — veteran commander at the Water Temple, and Krum's direct superior.
  • Charles Dammit — a guardsman turned deserter, now in disgrace.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — The guard fought and died in numbers across the Slums and the Water Temple, several withering to the thirsters' drought. The survivors, aided by the party, held the city — though they could not stop the priestess's abduction.

docs.title: The Bazaar
docs.text: The marketplace of Utsa Paradisa, where a bazaar ledger-man keeps the accounts. In an earlier session the party looted the Bazaar amid the chaos — and Behnsun Payne so frightened the ledger-man that he ate the ledger recording the stolen goods.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — Left ransacked but no longer under immediate threat, held by Major Jamieson and the remaining guards while the party moved on to other districts.

docs.title: The Jade District
docs.text: Also called the J District — a district of Utsa Paradisa and the home base of the city's Griffins. The party started their campaign here and cleared part of it early on, but the stronger enemy force has since concentrated against it.

docs.title: Notable Features
docs.text:
• The roost of the city's Griffins, defended by riders such as Seris.
  • The Water Temple, seat of the water priestess Naivara Tidewoven.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — Reported by Seris's aerial scouting as the most resilient district but under the heaviest attack. Seris flew to defend it while the party took the Slums first, then converged on the Water Temple here for the session's final battle.

docs.title: The Jade Pyramid
docs.text: The seat of Empress Serenity, a great stepped pyramid of green jade rising from the heart of the Jade District. Walls and a moat seal it off entirely but for a single tower on its south side, and its interior is woven through with illusion magic: corridors fold and mislead, so that even an intruder who slips inside cannot navigate its shifting halls without knowing the trick. Within, past hidden blood-keyed doors, it opens into a jade palace of green carpet and gold filigree, pillared galleries, and a council war room where the city's powers gather around the Empress's table.

docs.title: Notable Features
docs.text:
• The illusion-warped halls — turn one way and the path seems to veer another; outsiders are led in circles by design.
  • Blood-keyed doors — concealed entrances opened by a ring pressed to the wall, drawing a drop of the bearer's blood. Velra keeps one.
  • The war room — where Empress Serenity holds council, flanked by her bodyguard Horace Steelwinter.
  • Guest quarters — offered to the party for the night.

docs.title: Who You'll Find Here
docs.text: The Empress and her inner circle — Horace Steelwinter, the drow Velra, the guard leader Karza Sunhorn, and a rotating council of the city's power brokers.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Dalen Marr and Velra led the party through the pyramid's maze to report to the Empress's council. Amid the introductions, accusations, and an impromptu dance, Prance was formally charged with recovering Naivara Tidewoven.

docs.title: The Slums
docs.text: A poor district of Utsa Paradisa built inside the hollowed-out shells of ancient desert tortoises — "leviathan shells" from the giant beasts that once roamed this land, now repurposed as homes with shell "roofs" and elevated bridges between them.

docs.title: Notable Features
docs.text:
• An orphanage watched over by Behnsun Payne, home to the children Cadet Fox and Cadet Tiger.
  • A tavern run by the survivors of Behnsun's old crew.
  • The home of Adarius's parents.

docs.title: Who You'll Find Here
docs.text: Paddy Greenfoot the gnome, local guardsmen, and the common folk who make up Fizz's fanbase.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — The party chose to defend the Slums first, battling fire mephits, suture flies, and a thirster amid the tortoise shells. Adarius's father was gravely burned but survived; the Dragonborn Band arrived to turn the tide with music and healing. The district was left safe under Paddy Greenfoot and the guard.

docs.title: The University
docs.text: The University of Sand — a district of Utsa Paradisa home to the city's wizards, shaped like a great hourglass rising and cascading from the desert, its windows twisting up its sides in a helix. Every school of magic is taught here except necromancy. During the citywide assault it was the district that fared best, held by "a lot of strong wizards" — though at brutal cost: some nine or ten students and around fifteen guards fell defending it.

docs.title: Who You'll Find Here
docs.text: Krum's uncle, the divination professor Holgren, teaches here, and Adarius has connections among its scholars — soon to be a student himself on the Empress's scholarship. Its arcane affairs are overseen by Raasha Vaad and the war mage Seris.

docs.title: The Missing Students
docs.text:
Four gifted students who shared an off-campus dorm vanished in the chaos of the attack — neither among the dead nor found alive:

  • Cassian — human, evocation
  • Celine — half-elf, divination (a talented loner; Holgren's student)
  • Varicash — brass dragonborn, illusion
  • Calus — tiefling, conjuration

Their room showed no struggle and no detectable magic — because Celine had planted anti-divination devices to mask everything within, and left animated guardians behind.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — Reported intact by Seris's aerial scouting; shouts of victory rose from the Wizard Tower as the city was secured for the night.
  • The Vanished Scholars — The party came here to investigate the four missing students. They found Holgren battered among the dead, then entered the students' sealed dorm — where the diviner's animated guardians (a mimic, a swarm of flying books, and a smothering rug) nearly killed them all.

docs.title: The Water Temple
docs.text: The temple in the Jade District of Utsa Paradisa — also called the Veil of Tides — where the water priestess Naivara Tidewoven performs the rites that cleanse the city's water and keep it flowing. In a city where water is sacred and scarce, it is among the most vital sites in Utsa Paradisa. Its greatest rite is the Festival of the Four Currents, when Naivara's labor lets the city hand out extra water rations — which made the timing of the attack, on the eve of the festival, look chillingly deliberate.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — The session's climactic battle. The party arrived — famously, by catapulting one another across the battlefield — to find suture flies stitching Naivara's mouth and hands shut. The guard commander Dalen Marr held the line, but the flies carried the priestess out of the city. Before she vanished she dropped a teardrop amulet to the party — the session's central clue.
  • The Vanished Scholars — The party began the night outside its doors, and learned from the Empress just how much the city depends on Naivara: without her sanctifying the water, the dwindling supply grows perilous, and the festival hangs in the balance.

docs.title: Utsa Paradisa — the City of Exiles
docs.text: A desert-oasis city in the Northern Territories of Erratt, and the campaign's home base. See world.md for the full setting.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Utsa Paradisa is a haven for the exiled — Tieflings, Tabaxi, and other beastfolk cast out by long-dead nations — ruled by Empress Selene, whose diplomacy brokered the fragile peace between Drathomir and the Goliaths. Here water is sacred and scarce, heavily guarded, and whoever controls it holds power.

docs.title: Districts
docs.text:
• The Bazaar — ransacked marketplace, held by the guard.
  • The Slums — tortoise-shell dwellings; home to an orphanage, a tavern, and Adarius's parents.
  • The Jade District — home of the Griffins and the Water Temple; under the heaviest attack.
  • The University — defended by strong wizards.
  • The Luxury District — the upscale quarter, where Prance Galavant has made connections.

docs.title: Current State
docs.text: As of The Tidewoven Amulet, the city is in chaos — overrun by fey and elemental attackers (suture flies, thirsters, and fire mephits) in the aftermath of the previous session. The party fought district by district to beat back the assault, but the water priestess Naivara Tidewoven was abducted from the Water Temple. The city is "safe for now."

docs.title: Charles Dammit
docs.text: Role: Guardsman of the City Guard of Utsa Paradisa

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A city guard the party named in an earlier session, since revealed to be a coward. When the city came under attack he fled and hid rather than hold his post. Major Jamieson intends to make him an "office boy" as punishment, and Krum is no friend of his.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — Mentioned only; still missing, having abandoned the Bazaar during the chaos.

docs.title: Dalen Marr
docs.text: Role: Veteran commander of the City Guard of Utsa Paradisa

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A rugged, older guard commander — one of the elder officers, and the man Krum reports to directly. He fights with grim humor, standing his ground at the Water Temple and roaring at the attackers even when blinded by smoke: "I still see you, you pieces of shit." He knows the secret ways of the Jade Pyramid and the drow Velra who keeps them, and answers up the chain to the guard leader Karza Sunhorn. In court he keeps his place, speaking only when spoken to — though he can't help swaying when Fizz plays.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — Held the line at the Water Temple through the final battle, taking hits meant for the party and surviving the assault that carried off Naivara Tidewoven.
  • The Vanished Scholars — Led the party through the Jade Pyramid's hidden door and shifting halls to the Empress's council, where he vouched for Krum as worthy of the investigation.

docs.title: Empress Serenity
docs.text: Role: Empress of Utsa Paradisa · Seat: the Jade Pyramid

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The ruler of the City of Exiles, who holds court in the Jade Pyramid flanked by her Goliath bodyguard Horace Steelwinter. She is imperious and unabashedly vain — "the most important person in this city, and I do not say that lightly, because I am very, very important" — quick to humble a loud newcomer ("simmer down, young harengon; speak when you're spoken to") and quicker to end squabbling at her war table. Beneath the hauteur she is a shrewd diplomat: she is the one who brokered the fragile peace between the city and the dragonkin of Drathomir, and she reads the attack on her city as a calculated strike, timed to the Festival of the Four Currents.

Her one irreplaceable asset is the abducted water priestess Naivara Tidewoven, whose sanctification keeps the city's scarce water drinkable — which is why the priestess's loss frightens her more than she will admit, and why she formally charges the party with getting her back.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Received the party's report on the assault, dismissed her council, and made the rescue of Naivara Prance's official charge. Sweetened it for Adarius with a full scholarship to the University and a promise to move his parents somewhere better, then permitted the party — with Krum as their guard escort — to investigate the four missing students.

docs.title: Frederick
docs.text: Role: Talking fey amulet carried by Fizz

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Frederick is a talking wooden amulet — a fey being bound into an idol — that Fizz carries and converses with. Only Fizz can hear him, which makes for some one-sided conversations with a piece of wood. Frederick is crotchety and comic, quick to withhold his trust, and speaks fondly (and protectively) of someone he calls "mom."

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: • Recognized the spirit in Naivara Tidewoven's teardrop — the Amulet Speaker — as a "brother," and confirmed that Fizz, like Prance, has been "chosen" by a fey vessel.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — Vouched (grudgingly) for the new amulet and its quest, tying Fizz into the same fey mystery now driving Prance.

docs.title: Glidershade
docs.text: Role: Griffon of the Jade District · Rider: Seris

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The griffon ridden by Seris, and one of the beasts of the Griffin roost in the Jade District. Glidershade took a liking to the party after Prance so impressed the beast in an earlier session.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — Carried Seris on her aerial reconnaissance over the city, then flew with her to defend the Jade District against the heaviest of the assault.

docs.title: Gorvak Skybinder
docs.text: Role: Orc keeper of the Griffin hatchery, envoy of the Iron Holds

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The gruff orc who manages the city's Griffin hatchery — a gift to Utsa Paradisa from King Dumaville of the Iron Holds, with Gorvak stationed here to watch over it. An abrasive outsider, tolerated rather than trusted: he needled Adarius about his old job mucking out the Griffin stables, and jabbed that "maybe your jade god isn't as pure as you thought." The Empress makes no secret of her suspicion of him, reasoning aloud that the Iron Holds would not gift Griffins for free — and that if they had struck at the city, it would be to cripple it into dependence.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Sat the council as the Iron Holds' man, trading barbs with Adarius and sowing doubt, while the Empress quietly weighed whether his masters were behind the missing water shipment and the attack.

docs.title: Holgren
docs.text: Role: Divination professor at the University; Krum's uncle

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
An old dwarf who teaches divination at the University of Sand, and Krum's uncle — perpetually messy-bearded (blood, ketchup, mustard; no one can ever tell). He fought through the assault on the University and came out of it battered and near collapse, having lost some nine or ten students and around fifteen guards. Of the four missing students, only the diviner Celine was his; he remembered her as a gifted loner but, worn to the bone, could recall little more.

He handed Krum a bronze mirror backed with a Gorgon's face — a keepsake Krum had been given but "wasn't ready" for before. Now, looking into it, Krum glimpses a spectral second self behind his reflection, an echo of his Phantom nature.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Met the party amid the University's dead, gave what little he knew of the missing diviner Celine, and passed Krum the Gorgon-backed bronze mirror. He winced off Prance's "old fey remedy" of salt-in-the-wound before Krum could stop it.

docs.title: Horace Steelwinter
docs.text: Role: Goliath bodyguard to Empress Serenity

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A mountain of a Goliath — seven feet and change — who stands at the Empress's shoulder in the Jade Pyramid and rarely lets his stone face crack. He keeps her war room in order the direct way: when Salvatore Danilo propped his boots on the council table, Horace swept them off with the flat of his enormous hammer and a low "you will not disrespect our war room." Loyal and protective, he waves off the party as "these idiots" even as he promises the Empress they'll find Naivara. For all his stoicism, he proved a shockingly graceful dancer.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Kept order through the tense council. When Prance begged the last dance of the festival, Horace led it himself — and tangoed with such flawless skill (a natural 20) that the flamboyant rabbit-knight was left spun to the floor.

docs.title: Karza Sunhorn
docs.text: Role: Minotaur leader of the City Guard of Utsa Paradisa

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The minotaur who commands the city guard — the officer Dalen Marr reports to, and thus Krum's ultimate superior. Reluctant to thin the city's defenses by sending guards chasing after the missing priestess, she struck a compromise: the party could pursue the investigation so long as one of her own went with them. On Dalen's word that Krum was worthy, she assigned him as their escort — and, once the tension broke into dancing, asked her subordinate for a turn on the floor.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Authorized the party's investigation under guard escort, seconding Krum to them, and shared a dance with him before they left for the University.

docs.title: Major Jamieson
docs.text: Role: Officer of the City Guard of Utsa Paradisa

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A city guardsman who fell victim to the suture flies during the assault on Utsa Paradisa: his hands were sewn to his thighs and his lips stitched shut. The party found him panicking and freed him with a series of medicine checks and a healing touch.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Proud and duty-bound. The moment his mouth was freed — spitting blood — his first concern was rallying the remaining guards to hold the Bazaar. He has no patience for cowards: he wants the deserter Charles Dammit put to work as his "office boy" once the crisis passes.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — Freed by Fizz, Behnsun Payne, and Prance Galavant, who unstitched his mouth and hand and healed his wounds while Krum kept him calm.

docs.title: Naivara Tidewoven
docs.text: Role: Water Genasi priestess of Utsa Paradisa · Status: Abducted

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A water Genasi priestess and one of the most important figures in the City of Exiles — by the DM's own reckoning, "besides the Empress, she may be the most important person in the city." Naivara cleanses the water when it is corrupted and prays to the goddess of water to keep it flowing into Utsa Paradisa, a city where water is sacred and scarce.

docs.title: Appearance
docs.text: A fish-like water Genasi. When the party found her at the Water Temple, her fingers were already burning from the assault.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — Ambushed at the Water Temple by suture flies, which sewed her mouth and then her hands shut to stop her praying, and carried her bodily out of the city. As she was flown away, she tore a gold teardrop amulet from her chest and dropped it — deliberately — onto Prance Galavant's ear. The amulet holds a trapped fey being who calls her "my daughter" and begs the party to save her.

docs.title: Open Threads
docs.text:
• Where are the suture flies taking her, and why silence a water-priestess specifically?
  • The Amulet Speaker is her father. What is he, and how did he come to be trapped in the teardrop?

docs.title: Paddy Greenfoot
docs.text: Role: Gnome of the Slums

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A gnome and old friend of the party from the Slums. Once left injured and in pain, Paddy had earlier helped Adarius and Krum reach the district. Warm and irrepressible, he grumbles about being too old to fight ("I should've blown in four years — what the hell am I doing out here?") even as he throws himself into the defense.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — Fought alongside the party in the Slums and, when the battle turned, ran to shield the orphanage children. Afterward he pledged that he and the guards could hold the Slums, freeing the party to press on to the Water Temple.

docs.title: Raasha Vaad
docs.text: Role: Hadozi administrator of the arcane at the University

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A Hadozi ("monkey person," as the party less-than-delicately put it) who oversees arcane affairs at the University of Sand alongside the war mage Seris. She and Seris held back a grave concern at the council out of fear for the school's reputation, until pressed: four promising students, all sharing an off-campus dorm, had vanished in the chaos of the attack — neither counted among the dead nor found alive. Their rooms held no trace of a struggle and no detectable magic. Exhausted from the battle at the University, she escorted the party to the dorm and then, genuinely spent, handed over the key and went to rest.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Broke the news of the four missing students to the council, then led the party to their sealed dorm. Her "no detectable magic" turned out to be the students' own anti-divination devices at work — the room was anything but empty.

docs.title: Salvatore Danilo
docs.text: Role: Proprietor of the Lucky Scorpion, council member

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A silk-tongued man of leisure who runs the Lucky Scorpion — the city's casino and pleasure house — and keeps his own private guard. He is the only figure in the Empress's war room unbothered by the citywide catastrophe: feet on the council table, a chalice of wine in hand, needling the grim Goliath Horace Steelwinter to come "relax with the girls." He is acquainted with Prance, and vouched (loosely) that the party had performed in the wealthier districts. On his way out he pulled Behnsun Payne aside with a whispered offer of work — "once you're done here, I may have work for you, if you're interested."

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Lounged through the council enjoying Fizz's music, reported the Lucky Scorpion held its own in the attack, and privately propositioned Behnsun Payne for some unspecified job.

docs.title: Seris
docs.text: Role: Tiefling Griffin rider · Affiliation: the Griffin riders of the Jade District

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A tiefling Griffin rider, addressed with courtly deference as "M'lady," who rides her griffon Glidershade. She survived a brush with death in an earlier session — saved by Krum, while Prance so impressed her Griffin that the beast itself took a liking to the party.

She is more than a rider: a former commander turned war mage and professor at the University, she once served as Behnsun Payne's superior and helped rescue him and Adarius and bring them to the city years ago. She now sits on the Empress's council alongside the arcane administrator Raasha Vaad.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — At Prance's request, she took to the air and scouted the city (rolling a natural 20 on perception), reporting that the University stood strong, the Slums were worse off than usual, and the Jade District — home of the Griffins and the Water Temple — was under the heaviest attack. She then flew to defend the Jade District, sending the party toward the Slums.
  • The Vanished Scholars — Sat the Empress's council with Raasha Vaad, vouching for the party and helping bring the plight of the four missing students to light. Visibly angry, concerned, and nervous throughout.

docs.title: The Amulet Speaker
docs.text: Role: Fey being trapped in the Tidewoven amulet · Status: Bound to Prance Galavant

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A fey being imprisoned inside a gold, teardrop-shaped water amulet dropped by Naivara Tidewoven as she was abducted. It speaks only to whoever holds it to their ear — where one hears the sound of ocean waves — and it is, by its own account, Naivara's father.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Prickly, grief-stricken, and imperious. It rejected Adarius flatly ("you were not chosen") and instead chose Prance ("You will do. You must save my daughter"). When Adarius called it names, it snapped back: "I have feelings, and my daughter was just kidnapped. I'm having a bad day."

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Father of Naivara Tidewoven, the abducted water priestess.
  • Recognized by Frederick — Fizz's own fey amulet — as kin; the two spirits are "brothers," and Frederick confirmed that Fizz has also been "chosen."

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — Revealed by Adarius's identify as "something trapped inside." Chose Prance, who donned the amulet and swore an oath to rescue the priestess, feeling a spark of magic settle into place.

docs.title: The Dragonborn Band
docs.text: Role: Troupe of dragonborn musicians · Affiliation: wandering performers of Utsa Paradisa

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A troupe of dragonborn troubadours the party first crossed at a chariot race — a red dragonborn singer with an Earth-Wind-and-Fire soul to his voice, a big dragonborn drummer, and a blue dragonborn among them. Old rivals turned allies, they remember the party as "the fuckers that fixed dark hearts" and admit the chariot race "was well played."

docs.title: Abilities
docs.text: When they play, their music grants inspiration (a d6 to add to a roll) to nearby fighters — and, pooling their magic once a day, they can lay hands and heal the wounded. Members trade element-nicknames: Earth, a hulking brown-scaled healer; Fire; and Water, who took a shine to Prance Galavant.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — Arrived mid-battle in the Slums, buoying the party with inspiring music and healing Krum, Prance, and Adarius's badly burned father after the fight.

docs.title: Tirakar Sun
docs.text: Role: Owner of the arena, council member of Utsa Paradisa

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The proprietor of the city's fighting arena and a seat on the Empress's council. Where the rest of the room worried over the abducted priestess, Tirakar fretted about his own business — some of his caged monsters killed in the attack, others escaped, and a number of prisoners loosed into the city along with them. The Empress cut him off sharply for raising ledgers while Naivara was gone, but the loose monsters and escaped prisoners he mentioned are now problems prowling the streets.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Reported to the council that the assault had emptied part of his arena: dead beasts, escaped monsters, and freed prisoners now scattered through Utsa Paradisa.

docs.title: Tisk Tisk
docs.text: Role: Old Tabaxi overseer of the Bazaar

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: An aged, haggard Tabaxi who runs the city's market and sits on the Empress's council to speak for it. He and Behnsun Payne have history — Tisk takes one wary look at Payne before giving his report — but he proved a friend to the party in the end, sending them off with healing potions "with his regards" for their work in the marketplace. At the council he reported no significant losses at the Bazaar beyond ordinary looting, and named the guard Charles Dammit as the one who fled the battle.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Gave his account of the Bazaar to the council and flagged Charles Dammit's desertion. Later sent the party five potions of greater healing — which proved to be all that kept them alive in the students' dorm.

docs.title: Velra
docs.text: Role: Drow confidante and guardian of Empress Serenity

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A hooded drow woman who guards the Jade Pyramid's secret ways and never lets her guard down. She met the party at a concealed door in the pyramid wall, opening it with a blood-keyed ring, and led them through the pyramid's shifting, illusion-warped halls — corridors that fold and mislead anyone who doesn't know the trick. In the war room she trusts no one but the Empress, watching the whole council with a cool, appraising eye.

She takes a peculiar interest in Fizz: she licked the blood he'd tried to sneakily wipe from her ring-hand, later put a dagger to his throat with a smiling "you should not trust anyone, my dear mushroom — but I think you may be worth my time," and traded winks with him across the room. Whether that is affection, appraisal, or a warning, not even Fizz can tell.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Escorted the party into the Jade Pyramid and through its maze to the Empress, kept a knife-edged eye on the council, and began a wary, flirtatious game of cat-and-mouse with Fizz.

docs.title: Adarius
docs.text:
Player: Josh · Ancestry: Human · Class: Wizard

The party's arcane mind — sharp, skeptical, and rarely without a dry remark.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Adarius is the group's resident spellcaster and its loudest voice of caution. When the party recovered a mysterious talking amulet, it was Adarius who ritually cast identify on it — and Adarius who immediately wanted to sell the "talking asshole necklace" rather than answer its call.

docs.title: Ties to the City
docs.text: His parents live in the Slums of Utsa Paradisa — a hardy father the party came to know as "Bob" and a nimble mother. During the defense of the Slums, his father was caught in a magma creature's fire and badly burned, but survived thanks to the party and the healing magic of the Dragonborn Band. Adarius is also said to have connections at the University.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — Cast identify on the teardrop amulet dropped by Naivara Tidewoven, learning that "something is trapped inside" — a fey being that rejected him outright ("you were not chosen"). Spent the session urging the party to sell the amulet rather than take up its quest, and rolled a dirty nat 20 on Insight to remain thoroughly unconvinced.
  • The Vanished Scholars — Revealed his Bladesinger training, dancing through the fight while humming Pure Imagination. Led the investigation of the missing students' dorm, endured Gorvak Skybinder's jabs about his old stable job, and was rewarded by Empress Serenity with a full University scholarship and a promise to rehouse his parents. The trapped room nearly killed him — smothered unconscious by an animated rug before Fizz's healing word brought him back.

docs.title: Behnsun Payne
docs.text:
Player: Jonathan · Ancestry: Human · Class: Sorcerer

"It's Behnsun Payne — and healing is my game." A gruff sorcerer with a soft spot he'd rather not admit to.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Behnsun leans on chill touch, chromatic orb, and firebolt, and keeps a rapier for flourish. His spell list ran thin against the fire creatures plaguing the city — most of them shrugged off flame — which forced him to get creative with cold and necrotic damage.

docs.title: Ties to the City
docs.text: Behnsun's roots are in the Slums. He looks after an orphanage there — two children, Cadet Fox and Cadet Tiger, call him "dad" — and has history with an old crew who run a tavern in the district. Last session he frightened a bazaar ledger-man badly enough that the man ate the ledger recording the party's stolen goods.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — Helped free the stitched-together guard Major Jamieson, fought through the Slums to protect his orphanage, and finished a fire mephit with a well-chosen chromatic orb of cold that froze the creature before it could explode.
  • The Vanished Scholars — Showed his Wild Magic sorcery, quickening chromatic orbs with metamagic. Danced with the drow Velra and drew a private job offer from Salvatore Danilo. Spent the dorm ambush getting repeatedly clobbered by flying books, then landed the fiery blow that finally melted the mimic.

docs.title: Fizz
docs.text:
Player: Kevin · Ancestry: Myconid · Class: Bard

A friendly mushroom-man performer who measures success by how many friends he can make.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Fizz supports the party with bardic inspiration, song of rest, and a light crossbow, and carries a respectable medicine kit. He has a fanbase among the common folk of the Slums — "a lot of my customers," as he put it when the party chose where to make their stand.

docs.title: Frederick
docs.text: Fizz carries Frederick, a talking wooden amulet that houses a fey being. Over the course of the session it was revealed that Frederick has "chosen" Fizz — marking him, like Prance, as bound to a fey vessel and its purposes.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — Freed Major Jamieson's sewn-shut mouth with a delicate medicine check, felled a suture fly with a clean crossbow shot, and used Frederick to confirm that both he and Prance had been "chosen" by kindred fey spirits.
  • The Vanished Scholars — Leaned hard into his College of Eloquence gift: soothed the tense council with music, sweet-talked Horace Steelwinter into a gift of healing potions (persuasion 26), and began a wary flirtation with Velra, who put a dagger to his throat and decided he "may be worth my time." His rapport spores even let him eavesdrop on the Amulet Speaker. Ended the dorm brawl by decomposing and eating the defeated books.

docs.title: Krum
docs.text:
Player: Matt · Ancestry: Dwarf · Class: Rogue

A hardy dwarf rogue — low on hit points, high on nerve.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Krum fights with paired daggers and a crossbow, leaning on sneak attack and a rogue's cunning action to dart around the battlefield. He spent the session convinced he'd die in every encounter ("I made my peace with this") and came out the other side as its biggest hero.

docs.title: Ties to the City
docs.text: Krum has an uncle at the University, and is known to the guard — he reports directly to the veteran commander Dalen Marr. He is not on friendly terms with the coward Charles Dammit.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — Twice let the party build a makeshift catapult and launch him across the battlefield to crash down on fire mephits, driving them so far into the earth that their death-bursts barely singed him. Also calmed the panicking Major Jamieson long enough for the party to unstitch him.
  • The Vanished Scholars — Seconded by the guard leader Karza Sunhorn as the party's official escort (and shared a dance with his own boss). His uncle Holgren gave him a Gorgon-backed bronze mirror that reveals his Phantom's spectral second self. Spent most of the dorm fight grappled in a mimic's tongue, dropped unconscious, and was hauled back by Prance's last lay on hands.

docs.title: Prance Galavant
docs.text:
(pronounced Prawnse)

Player: Gary · Ancestry: Harengon · Class: Paladin

A theatrical rabbit-knight who narrates his own legend as he lives it — "the greatest of heroes is here to improve the situation greatly."

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Prance was once a radiant lordling of the Feywild, celebrated for wit and charisma — until hubris undid him. Entrusted with a dreamspun flute that could call forth moonbeams, he tried to bend its magic past Fey Law, and the door he opened for beauty let tyranny walk through first: an outsider used the breach to seize the court. Too proud to say sorry, he swore instead to win back his glory through deeds so marvelous the error would become legend. The Courts banished him to the Material Plane, stripped of immortality and reshaped into a small, comical Harengon still marked with lingering fey grace.

Now he fights as a paladin — two-handed longsword and split mail, healing allies with lay on hands, leaning on his rabbit traits for lucky footwork on failed saves and a knack for brutal critical hits — dressed in lacquered violet-and-azure samurai armor, face dyed in blue and silver, never wearing a helmet lest the crowd miss his face. He has taken up the wandering samurai's discipline as an echo of fey ideals: glory, drama, beautiful swordplay. Every fight is the next act of a saga, and beneath the bravado runs a real fear — that the story will not end well, and he will never be forgiven. Where others loot, Prance postures.

docs.title: In Character
docs.text:
Ideals — Redemption through heroic deeds; one hero's legend can lift everyone; wonders and dangers are meant to be uncovered.

Bonds — He aches to return to the Feywild, not as a fool but as a hero whose saga is admired. He carries an exile's keepsake: a wooden flute that plays only in moonlight.

Flaws — Hubris that goads him into reckless challenges; a compulsion to escalate any task into something grand, practicality be damned; reminders of his banishment leave him rattled and brooding.

"Bear witness, for legend sharpened its blade today!"

"Dull swords tell dull tales — let mine carve a tale worth telling."

"I opened a door for beauty. Regrettably, tyranny walked through it first."

docs.title: The Tidewoven Amulet
docs.text: When Naivara Tidewoven was carried off, she draped a teardrop amulet over Prance's ear as a deliberate clue. The fey being inside chose him — "You will do. You must save my daughter." Against Adarius's strong objections, Prance donned the amulet and swore an oath to rescue the priestess, feeling "a spark of magic click" as he put it on.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — Requested the aerial recon that set the party's course, delivered a 39-damage brutal-critical smashing hit in the Slums, was catapulted (with the rest) into the temple fight, and ended the night bound by oath to the amulet's quest.
  • The Vanished Scholars — Grandly presented the party to Empress Serenity — and was promptly humbled — then formally accepted her charge to rescue Naivara Tidewoven, "by blade and by my oath." Won the festival's last dance only to be tango-spun to the floor by Horace Steelwinter. In the dorm he called on the Amulet Speaker for armor of Agathys and spent his final lay on hands to drag Krum back from death.
